draft.title: Why Australia runs current account deficits
card: Australia has run a current account deficit for most of the last 50 years. This means the money flowing out for trade, income and transfers has been larger than the money flowing in.
Australia has tended to invest more than its households, firms and government save. The gap is filled by borrowing from overseas, and that matches a current account deficit.

Australia pays large amounts of interest and profits to foreign owners of its assets. This income outflow is usually the biggest part of the deficit, and it is often larger than any gap in goods and services.
Trade in goods and services can be in surplus, as it often is when export prices for minerals are high. The deficit can still remain because of the income paid abroad.
draft.remember: Australia invests more than it saves and pays income to foreign investors, so the current account is often in deficit.

a.q: Which is a main reason Australia has run current account deficits over a long period?
opts: It invests more than it saves and borrows the gap abroad
It saves more than it invests and lends the extra overseas
It has run a deficit in goods and services every year
It receives more income from abroad than it pays out
a.why: When a country invests more than it saves, the gap is funded by foreign money, and this matches a current account deficit. Saving more than investing would lead to a surplus, not a deficit.
a.clue: Think about where the money for extra investment comes from.

b.q: In one year, Australia earns a surplus on trade in goods and services because of high mineral prices. Its current account is still in deficit. What is the most likely reason?
opts: Large income payments to foreign investors exceed the surplus
Australia saved more than it invested during that year
Foreign investors stopped owning any Australian assets
Mineral exports are not counted in the current account
b.why: Interest and profits paid to foreign owners of Australian assets are a large outflow, and they can be bigger than a trade surplus. Mineral exports are part of the current account, so the last option is wrong.
b.clue: Look at the part of the account that is not about trade.
